headline: Nvidia is bringing its large DGX Station AI workstation to Windows, with 748 GB of memory and a release planned for Q4.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an official Nvidia announcement; the price is Wccftech's figure.
importance_line: What changed: developers who work in Windows can use a large AI workstation without moving to Linux, which matters most to enterprise developers; the 20-petaflop and memory figures are on paper, and the price is Wccftech's estimate, not an Nvidia figure.
summary: Wccftech reports that Nvidia has announced a Windows version of its DGX Station, a deskside AI workstation that until now ran only on Linux, built around a single GB300 'Blackwell Ultra' chip with 748 GB of memory in total. Nvidia plans a release in the fourth quarter of 2026 without naming an exact date, and Wccftech puts the price at around $100,000, similar to AMD's Threadripper Halo Station, which is due in 2027.
notes: Read in full. Price and 20-petaflop figure are Wccftech's; the Nvidia announcement itself is confirmed.
